prf:bring-trilog-imaginary-tate-rational:
Proof Proof of bring trilog imaginary tate rational. Via Kummer reflection formula.

Kummer reflection (Lewin 1991, Eq. 6.10): for z \notin (0, 1):

  \mathrm{Li}_3(z) - \mathrm{Li}_3(1/z)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{\log^3(-z)}{6}
  - \frac{\pi^2 \log(-z)}{6}.

Apply at z = \zeta_5 = e^{2\pi i / 5}.

LHS. \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5) - \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^{-1}) = \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5) - \overline{\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5)} = 2 i\,\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5) = 2 i\,S_3(2\pi/5).

RHS. The principal-branch logarithm of -\zeta_5:

  -\zeta_5 \;=\; e^{i (2\pi/5 + \pi)} \;=\; e^{i \cdot 7\pi/5}.

Since 7\pi/5 > \pi, principal logarithm reduces mod 2\pi:

  \log(-\zeta_5) \;=\; i\,(7\pi/5 - 2\pi) \;=\; -\frac{3 i \pi}{5}.

Compute:

  \begin{aligned}
    \log^3(-\zeta_5) &\;=\; \left(-\tfrac{3 i \pi}{5}\right)^3 \;=\; \frac{27 i \pi^3}{125}, \\
    -\frac{\log^3(-\zeta_5)}{6} - \frac{\pi^2 \log(-\zeta_5)}{6}
    &\;=\; -\frac{27 i \pi^3}{750} + \frac{3 i \pi^3}{30} \\
    &\;=\; i \pi^3 \left( -\tfrac{9}{250} + \tfrac{25}{250} \right)
    \;=\; \frac{16 i \pi^3}{250}
    \;=\; \frac{8 i \pi^3}{125}.
  \end{aligned}

Combine. 2 i\,S_3(2\pi/5) = 8 i \pi^3 / 125, so S_3(2\pi/5) = 4 \pi^3 / 125. \square
prop:cl3-zeta5-orbit-sum-identity:
Proposition Cl_3(2\pi/5) + Cl_3(4\pi/5) = -(12/25)\zeta(3) — depth-3 reduces to a 1-dim antisymmetric generator. The real-part orbit sum evaluates explicitly:

  \mathrm{Cl}_3\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{5}\right)
  \;+\;
  \mathrm{Cl}_3\!\left(\tfrac{4\pi}{5}\right)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{12}{25} \cdot \zeta(3).

The Tate-rational imaginary parts reduce the unproved depth-3 elements. The orbit-sum identity further constrains the real parts to the \zeta(3)-line. Only the antisymmetric difference \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) - \mathrm{Cl}_3(4\pi/5) survives as the independent, genuinely new depth-3 element of the regulator image.
prf:cl3-zeta5-orbit-sum-identity:
Proof Proof of cl3 zeta5 orbit sum identity. Step 1 (multiplication formula). The classical N-th roots-of-unity multiplication identity for \mathrm{Li}_n:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_N^k)
  \;=\;
  \bigl( N^{1 - n} - 1 \bigr) \cdot \zeta(n).

For N = 5, n = 3:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{4} \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{24}{25} \cdot \zeta(3).

Step 2 (real part). Take real parts of both sides.

LHS: \sum_k \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^k) = \sum_k \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/5).

By the parity \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi - \theta) = \mathrm{Cl}_3(\theta) (since \cos is 2\pi-periodic and even):

  \mathrm{Cl}_3(8\pi/5) \;=\; \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Cl}_3(6\pi/5) \;=\; \mathrm{Cl}_3(4\pi/5).

So LHS = 2 (\mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) + \mathrm{Cl}_3(4\pi/5)).

RHS: \zeta(3) \in \mathbb{R}, so RHS = -24\zeta(3)/25.

Step 3 (combine).

  2 (\mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) + \mathrm{Cl}_3(4\pi/5))
  \;=\;
  -\frac{24}{25} \zeta(3),

giving the boxed sum identity. \square
prop:cl3-zeta5-pslq-independence:
Proposition PSLQ certifies Cl_3(2\pi/5) - Cl_3(4\pi/5) is independent of standard depth-3 periods up to coefficient norm 10^8. PSLQ searches at 70 decimal places with a coefficient norm bound of 10^8 certify that the difference

  X \;:=\; \mathrm{Cl}_3\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi}{5}\right) - \mathrm{Cl}_3\!\left(\tfrac{4\pi}{5}\right)
  \;\approx\; 0.955723\ldots

admits no \mathbb{Q}-linear relation with any standard weight-3 period basis elements.

The test subjects X against candidate bases including \{\zeta(3), \pi^3\} and full golden-ratio logarithmic bases. No relation emerges. While not a proof of irreducibility, the negative PSLQ result provides the strongest unconditional canonical evidence that X constitutes a genuinely independent depth-3 period. The depth-3 surface for \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5) reduces to this single real period.

What is proved is the identification of X: the coefficient \cos(2\pi n/5) - \cos(4\pi n/5) equals \tfrac{\sqrt5}{2}\,\chi_5(n), where \chi_5 is the quadratic character modulo 5, so

  X \;=\; \tfrac{\sqrt5}{2}\, L(3, \chi_5),
  \qquad L(3, \chi_5) \;=\; \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{\chi_5(n)}{n^3}.

The \mathbb{Q}-linear independence of L(3,\chi_5) from \zeta(3) and \pi^3 is not known; the PSLQ result is evidence for it, not a proof.

Comparison with the standard-relation dimension bound for \mathrm{MPV}(3,5) clarifies the scope of the candidate basis. At weight 3 and prime level N = 5, the 5^2(5+1) = 150 multiple polylogarithm values satisfy Deligne and Goncharov's motivic upper bound d(3,5) \le D(3,5) = (\varphi(5)/2 + 1)^3 = 27, which finite and regularized double-shuffle relations together with lifted weight-1 relations tighten to d(3,5) \le \mathrm{SR}(3,5) = 22 = (5^3 + 4\cdot 5^2 + 5\cdot 5 + 14)/12 [zhao2010-standard-relations, \S\S 7.3--7.4, \S 9 Table 2, Conj. 9.2]. Of the eight periods tested against X = \tfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2} L(3,\chi_5) \in \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{MPV}(3,5), the five level-1 and level-5 terms \{\zeta(3), \pi^3, \pi\log^2\varphi, \log^3\varphi, \pi^2\log\varphi\} span the real level-1 line and decomposable lower-weight products inside \mathrm{MPV}(3,5), while \{\pi\log^2 2, \pi^2\log 2, \log^3 2\} test cross-level independence against level 2; the remaining dimension up to \mathrm{SR}(3,5) = 22 accommodates X alongside imaginary parity components and higher-depth generators L_5(2,1\mid \cdot) and L_5(1^3\mid \cdot).
prop:cyclotomic-trilog-imaginary-closed-:
Proposition Trilogarithm imaginary part at \zeta_n: closed form (n - 1)(n - 2)\pi^3 / (3 n^3) for every root of unity. For every n \geq 1, the imaginary part of the depth-3 trilogarithm at roots of unity evaluates to:

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_n)
  \;=\;
  \frac{(n - 1)(n - 2)\,\pi^3}{3\,n^3}.

The evaluation remains Tate-rational for all n, projecting identically to zero under the Beilinson regulator quotient.

This extends the \zeta_5 result globally. Every cyclotomic depth-3 imaginary part resides in \pi^3 \mathbb{Q}. The genuinely new content at \zeta_n resides entirely within the real part \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/n) and its Galois conjugates. This halves the depth-3 surface dimension for every cyclotomic field. The asymptotic decay behaves as \pi^3 / 3n.

prf:cyclotomic-trilog-imaginary-closed-f:
Proof Proof of cyclotomic trilog imaginary closed form. Step 1 (Kummer reflection). For z \notin (0, 1) (Lewin 1991, Eq. 6.10):

  \mathrm{Li}_3(z) - \mathrm{Li}_3(1/z)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{\log^3(-z)}{6} - \frac{\pi^2 \log(-z)}{6}.

Step 2 (principal log of -\zeta_n). For n \geq 2, \zeta_n = e^{2\pi i/n} and

  -\zeta_n \;=\; e^{i (2\pi/n + \pi)}
  \;=\; e^{i\,\theta_n}, \quad \theta_n := 2\pi/n + \pi.

Since \theta_n > \pi for n \geq 2, the principal branch gives

  \log(-\zeta_n) \;=\; i\,(\theta_n - 2\pi)
  \;=\; i\pi \cdot \frac{2 - n}{n}.

(For n = 1, \zeta_1 = 1 and \mathrm{Li}_3(1) = \zeta(3) is real, so \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_1) = 0 — consistent with the formula at n = 1: (0)(-1) = 0.)

Step 3 (substitute and simplify). Write \alpha := (2 - n)/n, so \log(-\zeta_n) = i\pi\alpha and \log^3(-\zeta_n) = -i\pi^3\alpha^3.

  \begin{aligned}
    -\frac{\log^3(-\zeta_n)}{6} - \frac{\pi^2 \log(-\zeta_n)}{6}
    &\;=\;
    \frac{i\pi^3\alpha^3}{6} - \frac{i\pi^3\alpha}{6} \\
    &\;=\;
    \frac{i\pi^3 \alpha (\alpha^2 - 1)}{6}.
  \end{aligned}

Since \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_n^{-1}) = \overline{\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_n)}:

  \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_n) - \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_n^{-1})
  \;=\; 2 i\,\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_n).

Therefore

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_n)
  \;=\; \frac{\pi^3 \alpha (\alpha^2 - 1)}{12}.

Step 4 (factor in n). With \alpha = (2-n)/n:

  \alpha^2 - 1 \;=\; \frac{(2-n)^2 - n^2}{n^2} \;=\; \frac{4 - 4n}{n^2}
  \;=\; \frac{-4(n-1)}{n^2}.

So

  \alpha(\alpha^2 - 1)
  \;=\; \frac{2-n}{n} \cdot \frac{-4(n-1)}{n^2}
  \;=\; \frac{4(n-1)(n-2)}{n^3}.

Substituting:

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_n)
  \;=\; \frac{\pi^3}{12} \cdot \frac{4(n-1)(n-2)}{n^3}
  \;=\; \frac{(n-1)(n-2)\,\pi^3}{3\,n^3}.

\square
prop:cyclotomic-cl3-orbit-sum-general:
Proposition General orbit-sum identity: \sum_k \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N) = -(N^2-1)/N^2 \cdot \zeta(3) at every N \geq 2. For all N \geq 2, the real-part orbit sum reduces to:

  \sum_{k=1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Cl}_3\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi k}{N}\right)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{N^2 - 1}{N^2} \cdot \zeta(3).

For every cyclotomic field \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N), the real-part orbit sum collapses to a rational multiple of the classical \zeta(3). The genuinely new content resides entirely in the individual \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N) values modulo this sum. Combining this with the Tate-rationality of the imaginary parts reduces the depth-3 surface to at most \lfloor (N - 1)/2 \rfloor - 1 genuinely new real numbers.

prf:cyclotomic-cl3-orbit-sum-general:
Proof Proof of cyclotomic cl3 orbit sum general. Step 1 (multiplication formula). The classical N-th roots-of-unity multiplication identity for \mathrm{Li}_n:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_N^k)
  \;=\;
  \bigl( N^{1 - n} - 1 \bigr) \cdot \zeta(n).

For n = 3:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_N^k)
  \;=\;
  \bigl( N^{-2} - 1 \bigr)\, \zeta(3)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{N^2 - 1}{N^2}\, \zeta(3).

Step 2 (take real part). \zeta(3) \in \mathbb{R} is real. \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_N^k) = \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N) by definition.

Therefore

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{N^2 - 1}{N^2}\, \zeta(3).

Step 3 (parity reduction for odd N). By \mathrm{Cl}_3 parity:

  \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi (N - k)/N)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi - 2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N).

For odd N, the indices k = 1, \ldots, N - 1 pair as (k, N - k), giving (N - 1)/2 pairs. Therefore

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  2 \sum_{k = 1}^{(N - 1)/2} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N),

and dividing by 2:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{(N - 1)/2} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{N^2 - 1}{2 N^2}\, \zeta(3).

For even N, the middle term k = N/2 gives \mathrm{Cl}_3(\pi) = \sum_{j \geq 1} \cos(j\pi)/j^3 = \sum_{j \geq 1} (-1)^j/j^3 = -\frac{3}{4}\zeta(3) (alternating Dirichlet series for \zeta(3)), and the other (N - 2)/2 pairs contribute symmetrically. The closed form then takes the form recorded above (N = 2 in the table below verifies -\frac{3}{4}\zeta(3) directly). \square
conj:cyclotomic-depth3-dimension-synthes:
Conjecture Cyclotomic depth-3 dimension synthesis: (K - 3)/2 at every prime K \geq 5. For prime K \geq 5, let \mathcal{V}_K \subseteq \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathcal{P}_2 be the \mathbb{Q}-vector space spanned by the depth-3 grouplikes at the \zeta_K-orbit modulo the \zeta(3)-line. The vector space dimension is conjectured to be:

  \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} \mathcal{V}_K
  \;=\;
  \frac{K - 3}{2}.

The Tate-rational imaginary parts contribute zero dimension. The real-part orbit sum absorbs one dimension into the \zeta(3)-line. The remaining real parts supply at most (K-3)/2 dimensions. Equality needs these real parts to be \mathbb{Q}-linearly independent, which is the open Beilinson–Zagier conjecture for \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_K).

rem:cyclotomic-depth3-dimension-synthesi:
Remark Upper-bound sketch for cyclotomic depth3 dimension synthesis. Sketch.

Step 1 (count starting generators). The cyclotomic Galois orbit of \zeta_K consists of \varphi(K) = K - 1 primitive Kth roots of unity. Grouped by complex-conjugate pairs (since \overline{\zeta_K^j} = \zeta_K^{K-j}), the orbit yields (K - 1)/2 pairs.

For each pair \{\zeta_K^j, \zeta_K^{K-j}\}, the corresponding \mathrm{Li}_3 values give:

  • One real part \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi j/K) = \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_K^j) (bar-fixed in \mathcal{P}_3^+).
  • One imaginary part S_3(2\pi j/K) = \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_K^j) (bar-twisted in \mathcal{P}_3^-, related to its conjugate by sign).

Total: (K - 1)/2 real parts + (K - 1)/2 imaginary parts = K - 1 candidate generators.

Step 2 (eliminate imaginary parts via Theorem A). By Trilogarithm imaginary part at \zeta_n: closed form (n - 1)(n - 2)\pi^3 / (3 n^3) for every root of unity:

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_K^j)
  \;=\;
  \frac{(jK - 1)(jK - 2)\,\pi^3}{3\,(jK)^3}
  \quad \text{(?)}

Wait — the formula applies at \zeta_n with n = K/\gcd(j, K). For prime K and 1 \leq j \leq K - 1, \gcd(j, K) = 1, so \zeta_K^j is itself a primitive Kth root. Apply Theorem A at n = K:

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_K^j)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{sign}(\ldots) \cdot
  \frac{(K - 1)(K - 2)\,\pi^3}{3\,K^3} \cdot (\text{sign from } j).

More precisely: \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_K^j) = S_3(2\pi j/K) where S_3 is bounded in magnitude by the closed-form expression (K - 1)(K - 2)\pi^3/(3K^3) at the principal angle. By the multi-angle Tate-rational structure (Step 1 above), every imaginary part is a \mathbb{Q}-linear combination of \pi^3 — i.e., lies in the 1-dim Tate-line \pi^3 \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathcal{P}_3.

Under the Beilinson regulator quotient \mathcal{P}_3 \to \mathcal{P}_3 / \mathrm{Tate}, all (K - 1)/2 imaginary parts collapse to zero. They contribute zero dimensions to \mathcal{V}_K.

Step 3 (count residual real-part dimensions). The (K - 1)/2 real parts \{\mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi j/K) : 1 \leq j \leq (K - 1)/2\} satisfy:

  • Orbit-sum relation by General orbit-sum identity: \sum_k \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi k/N) = -(N^2-1)/N^2 \cdot \zeta(3) at every N \geq 2:

      \sum_{j=1}^{(K - 1)/2} \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi j/K)
  \;=\;
  -\frac{K^2 - 1}{2K^2}\,\zeta(3).

    This is one linear relation modulo \mathcal{V}_K — it pulls a 1-dim component into the \zeta(3)-line, which projects to zero in \mathcal{P}_3 / (\mathcal{P}_2 + \mathbb{Q}\zeta(3)).

Therefore the remaining \mathbb{Q}-rank of the real parts modulo \mathcal{V}_K is at most:

  \frac{K - 1}{2} - 1 \;=\; \frac{K - 3}{2}.

Step 4. Combining Steps 2 (imaginary parts contribute 0) and 3 (real parts contribute at most (K - 3)/2):

  \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} \mathcal{V}_K \;\leq\; \frac{K - 3}{2}.

\square
prop:jonquiere-cyclotomic-tate-rationali:
Proposition General Jonquière Tate-rationality: wrong-parity part of \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) has closed form -(2\pi i)^n / n! \cdot B_n(1/K) at every depth. For every depth n \geq 2, the wrong-parity part of \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) obeys a uniform Bernoulli-polynomial closed form:

  \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) - (-1)^{n - 1}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K^{-1})
  \;=\;
  -\frac{(2\pi i)^n}{n!} \cdot B_n\!\left(\tfrac{1}{K}\right).

The wrong-parity part—the imaginary part for odd n and real part for even n—evaluates as Tate-rational at every depth. It contributes zero to the Beilinson regulator image. The genuinely new period content isolates precisely to the right-parity part. This dictates why the depth-2 imaginary \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2 and the depth-3 real \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_3 carry the true periods.
prf:jonquiere-cyclotomic-tate-rationalit:
Proof Proof of jonquiere cyclotomic tate rationality. Step 1 (Jonquière inversion formula, Lewin 1991 §7). For z \notin (0, 1) and n \geq 1:

  \mathrm{Li}_n(z) \;=\; (-1)^{n - 1}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(z^{-1})
  \;-\; \frac{(2\pi i)^n}{n!} B_n\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2} + \tfrac{\log(-z)}{2\pi i}\right),

where the principal branch of \log is taken.

Step 2 (specialise at z = \zeta_K = e^{2\pi i/K}, K \geq 2). Here -\zeta_K = e^{i (2\pi/K + \pi)}. For K \geq 2, the angle 2\pi/K + \pi exceeds \pi, so the principal log subtracts 2\pi:

  \log(-\zeta_K) \;=\; i\pi (2 - K)/K.

Compute the Bernoulli argument:

  \frac{1}{2} + \frac{\log(-\zeta_K)}{2\pi i}
  \;=\; \frac{1}{2} + \frac{2 - K}{2K}
  \;=\; \frac{K + (2 - K)}{2K}
  \;=\; \frac{1}{K}.

The Bernoulli polynomial evaluates at 1/K — a particularly clean specialisation. Substituting into Step 1:

  \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) - (-1)^{n - 1}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K^{-1})
  \;=\;
  -\frac{(2\pi i)^n}{n!}\,B_n(1/K).

Step 3 (extract real / imaginary part on unit circle). Since \zeta_K^{-1} = \overline{\zeta_K}, \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K^{-1}) = \overline{\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K)}.

  • n odd: (-1)^{n - 1} = 1. LHS = \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) - \overline{\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K)} = 2 i\,\mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K).
  • n even: (-1)^{n - 1} = -1. LHS = \mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) + \overline{\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K)} = 2\,\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K).

Therefore:

  \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) \;=\; -\frac{(2\pi i)^n}{2 i \cdot n!}\,B_n(1/K), \qquad n \text{ odd},
  \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Li}_n(\zeta_K) \;=\; -\frac{(2\pi i)^n}{2 \cdot n!}\,B_n(1/K), \qquad n \text{ even}.

Both expressions are rational multiples of \pi^n — Tate-rational. \square
prop:cyclotomic-orbit-sum-all-depths:
Proposition General orbit-sum at every depth: \sum_k \mathrm{Cl}_n(2\pi k/N) = (N^{1-n} - 1)\zeta(n) for n odd, 0 for n even. For all depths n \geq 2, the orbit sum evaluates as:

  \sum_{k = 1}^{N - 1} \mathrm{Cl}_n\!\left(\tfrac{2\pi k}{N}\right)
  \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    \bigl(N^{1 - n} - 1\bigr)\, \zeta(n) & \text{\(n\) odd}, \\[4pt]
    0 & \text{\(n\) even}.
  \end{cases}

For odd depths, the sum isolates exactly one dimension of classical \zeta(n) content. For even depths, the antisymmetric values pair-cancel, leaving all (N-1)/2 magnitudes independent. The dimension count strictly bifurcates by parity: (K-3)/2 for odd depths, and (K-1)/2 for even depths.

conj:cyclotomic-dimension-synthesis-all-:
Conjecture Cyclotomic dimension synthesis at every depth: (K - 3)/2 for n odd, (K - 1)/2 for n even. For every prime K \geq 3 and depth n \geq 2, the dimension of the \mathbb{Q}-vector space \mathcal{V}_{n, K} spanning the genuinely new depth-n grouplikes is conjectured to be:

  \dim_{\mathbb{Q}}\mathcal{V}_{n, K}
  \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    (K - 3)/2 & \text{\(n\) odd}, \\
    (K - 1)/2 & \text{\(n\) even}.
  \end{cases}

This extends the count to every depth. The Tate-rationality clears the wrong-parity parts. The orbit sum handles the classical \zeta(n) contributions. The counting gives these values as upper bounds; equality is Beilinson's prediction and is open.

prop:cyclotomic-strand-doubling:
Proposition Cyclotomic doubling identity: \Phi_8(X) = \Phi_4(X^2). Over \mathbb{Z}[X], the cyclotomic polynomials satisfy:

  \Phi_8(X) \;=\; \Phi_4(X^2).

A computed observation about atomic-step Habiro elements that motivated this identity is recorded in this remark.
rem:cyclotomic-strand-doubling-habiro-ob:
Remark The \Phi_8^2 prefactor observed in atomic-step Habiro elements. This remark records a computed observation that motivated the identity \Phi_8(X) = \Phi_4(X^2). It is an observation about computed examples, not part of the identity.

Universal atomic-step cyclotomic. The Habiro elements for successive atomic-step pairs—from deuteron to helium—universally extract a \Phi_8^2 cyclotomic prefactor. The appearance of \Phi_8 precedes the mechanical m=8 Pochhammer boundary, confirming it as a structural interference signature amongst the Habiro coefficients themselves.

The prior hypothesis interpreting X \mapsto X^2 as a categorical strand-doubling map failed empirical tests. The substitution does not generate a powers-of-two cyclotomic tower for heavier nuclei. The algebraic identity remains valid, but the categorical mechanism producing the universal \Phi_8^2 signature remains open.
prf:cyclotomic-strand-doubling: Proof Proof of cyclotomic strand doubling. By direct evaluation, \Phi_4(X) = X^2 + 1 and \Phi_8(X) = X^4 + 1. Composing \Phi_4 with X^2 gives (X^2)^2 + 1 = X^4 + 1 = \Phi_8(X). ∎
prop:a-8-partition-function-identity:
Proposition Habiro coefficient a_8(X) partition-function identity: a_8(X) = \sum_{n=1}^{5} p(n)\,X^{5-n}. Let a_8 \in \mathbb{Z}[X] denote the top-shared (m = 8) integer Habiro coefficient of the proton and neutron in the canonical Habiro-witness convention:

  a_8(X) \;=\; X^4 + 2\,X^3 + 3\,X^2 + 5\,X + 7.

Then a_8 admits the closed form

  a_8(X) \;=\; \sum_{n=1}^{5} p(n)\,X^{5-n},

where p(n) denotes the integer partition function (Hardy–Ramanujan, OEIS A000041): p(1) = 1,\; p(2) = 2,\; p(3) = 3,\; p(4) = 5,\; p(5) = 7.
prf:a8-partition-function-identity:
Proof Proof of a8 partition function identity. Coefficient-by-coefficient match in descending order of X-power:

Power of X Coefficient in a_8 p(n) n = 5 - k
X^4 1 p(1) = 1 (match) n = 1
X^3 2 p(2) = 2 (match) n = 2
X^2 3 p(3) = 3 (match) n = 3
X^1 5 p(4) = 5 (match) n = 4
X^0 7 p(5) = 7 (match) n = 5

Each coefficient is the exact value of the integer partition function at the corresponding index. The identity is checked in \mathbb{Z}[X] by direct polynomial expansion of \sum_{n=1}^{5} over \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}. ∎
prop:zeta8-witness-level2-su2:
Proposition Level-2 SU(2) Verlinde witness at q = \zeta_8: (\zeta_8;\zeta_8)_7 = 8, \mathrm{ord}(\sigma_i) = 8, [4]_q = 0, and the Wenzl annihilator. Let \zeta be a primitive 8th root of unity in a field R,

  \zeta_8 = e^{i\pi/4} \in \mathbb{C} \quad (\text{analytic model}).

Then the following three algebraic facts hold:

  1. (\zeta_8;\zeta_8)_7 \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{7}\,(1 - \zeta_8^k) \;=\; 8.
  2. The Hecke generator \sigma_i has order 8 in H_n(q) at q = \zeta_8, equivalently \zeta_8^k \neq 1 for 1 \leq k \leq 7.
  3. The quantum integer [4]_q := (q^4 - q^{-4})/(q - q^{-1}) vanishes at q = \zeta_8.

Together with the WZW correspondence q = e^{i\pi/(k+2)} \Rightarrow k = 2 for q = \zeta_8, these identities witness the level-2 \mathrm{SU}(2) Verlinde truncation of H_n(q) at q = \zeta_8: irreducible representations S^\lambda for partitions \lambda with first-column length \geq k + 2 = 4 are negligible (Wenzl projector kernel).
prf:zeta8-witness-level2-su2:
Proof Proof of zeta8 witness level2 su2. (1) From the cyclotomic factorisation X^8 - 1 \;=\; \prod_{k=0}^{7}\,(X - \zeta_8^k), dividing by (X - 1) gives X^7 + X^6 + \cdots + 1 \;=\; \prod_{k=1}^{7}\,(X - \zeta_8^k). Evaluating at X = 1: LHS = 8 and RHS = \prod_{k=1}^{7}\,(1 - \zeta_8^k) = (\zeta_8;\zeta_8)_7, so (\zeta_8;\zeta_8)_7 = 8. ∎

(2) Since \zeta_8 = e^{2\pi i / 8} is a primitive 8th root of unity, \zeta_8^k = 1 iff 8 \mid k, so \zeta_8^k \neq 1 for 1 \leq k \leq 7. The Hecke quadratic relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 at q = \zeta_8 gives eigenvalues \sigma_i \in \{\zeta_8, -\zeta_8^{-1}\}. Both eigenvalues have order 8: \zeta_8 directly, and -\zeta_8^{-1} = \zeta_8^4 \cdot \zeta_8^{-1} = \zeta_8^3 which is also a primitive 8th root of unity. The order of \sigma_i is therefore \mathrm{lcm}(8, 8) = 8. ∎

(3) At q = \zeta_8, q^4 = (e^{i\pi/4})^4 = e^{i\pi} = -1, so q^4 = -1 = q^{-4}, giving q^4 - q^{-4} = 0. Since q - q^{-1} \neq 0 (as \zeta_8 \neq \pm 1), [4]_q = 0/(q - q^{-1}) = 0. ∎
sec:nuclear-binding-beta-stability-intro:
Arc III transitions from single-link hyperbolic volumes to many-body nuclear binding. In a composite nucleus of mass number A, the constituent nucleons interact through an A-strand braid whose Markov trace decomposes over the Wedderburn blocks V_\lambda of H_A(q). At each jet filtration level \ell, the effective coupling of block V_\lambda is determined by the linear-programming shadow price of the Frobenius positivity constraint, expressed in closed form through elementary symmetric polynomials in the Jucys–Murphy central elements.

This section sets up the substrate binding architecture. It derives the confined knot-binding decomposition and the Wigner np-pairing weight, establishes the exchange-criticality algebra of the q-Reeb pn-bond, and connects the canonical Wedderburn weights to the hook-length and Wigner coefficients. Once the mass coefficients are identified as shadow prices, the dominant \beta-decay channel of an unstable atom is characterised as the unique Wedderburn shadow-price constraint violated at the phase boundary. Finally, it proves that Frobenius self-duality of the Iwahori–Hecke algebra forces the binding coefficients to be extracted via the LP-dual shadow-price program, unifying the iterative mass-formula corrections into a single convex-duality scheme.
prop:wedderburn-weight-canonical:
Proposition Canonical q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight \tilde w_\lambda and named scalings (BW, LP for all \lambda). The Bethe-Weizsäcker mass coefficient and the LP shadow-price scale the identical canonical q-deformed Wedderburn-block weight:

  \tilde w_\lambda(q)
  \;:=\;
  \frac{\dim_q(\lambda)^2}{[n]_q!}.

The quantum hook-length dimension \dim_q(\lambda) is defined by the q-deformed Frame-Robinson-Thrall formula. This identity holds for all \lambda. No relation between the Markov coefficient y_\lambda and \tilde w_\lambda is asserted: the former "Wenzl-bridge reduction" y_\lambda = \tilde w_\lambda(q) on the self-conjugate stratum is false there and was dropped (see below).

This establishes the central canonicity of the weight \tilde w_\lambda(q). The LP form multiplies this weight by h/2. The Markov coefficient y_\lambda, given by Wenzl's hook-content closed form, is a distinct family on every stratum.

Failure of the Wenzl-bridge premise on the \kappa_\lambda = 0 stratum. The identity y_\lambda = \tilde w_\lambda for \kappa_\lambda = \sum_x c(x) = 0 fails at every such partition with n \leq 6 except the trivial one-cell \lambda = (1):

\lambda \kappa y_\lambda(q_0) \tilde w(q_0)
(1) 0 1.00000000 1.00000000
(2,1) 0 0.24729789 0.66067377
(2,2) 0 0.06115624 0.16604895
(3,1,1) 0 0 0.29466896
(3,2,1) 0 0 0.35863564

(2,2) and (3,2,1) are precisely the two partitions this block's cited script is said to have verified.

The last two rows are a scope-(b) structural exclusion, not a numerical near-miss. The Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) is the \mathfrak{sl}_2 point of the Ocneanu family (Reconciliation of the Markov parameter z), so y_\lambda = 0 identically once \lambda has more than two rows — such a \lambda has a cell of content -2, whose Ocneanu numerator factor vanishes. Meanwhile \tilde w_\lambda is a ratio of products of positive quantum integers, hence strictly positive for q > 0. The identity there asserts 0 = \text{positive}, and no choice of parameter reconciles it. The other two rows are scope (a): measured non-equality under six readings of \dim_q(\lambda)^2/[n]_q! (symmetric vs unbalanced quantum integer, q-deformed vs ordinary dimension, squared vs unsquared), none of which matches.

What this does not invalidate, which is most of the block. The identity y_\lambda = \tilde w_\lambda on self-conjugate partitions was only ever assumed, never proved, so no proved statement is made wrong by its falsity; results conditional on it were vacuous at the intended weights rather than false. The BW and LP scalings \beta_\lambda = -\tfrac12 \tilde w_\lambda and C_\lambda = \tilde w_\lambda \cdot h/2 stand as definitional, and the relation \beta_\lambda h = -C_\lambda follows from them alone, without the identity. The block's own off-stratum statement, that y_\lambda and \tilde w_\lambda are genuinely distinct families, is correct — and on this evidence correct on the stratum too.

Disposition: dropped as a hypothesis. Of the three options — restrict the identity to \lambda = (1), drop it, or demote the block to a conjecture — the author chose to drop. The weights y_\lambda are retained as data only, with no asserted relation to \tilde w_\lambda. The two definitional scalings and the relation \beta_\lambda h = -C_\lambda are unchanged.

Notation. This block's weight is \tilde w_\lambda, the third of the three registered partition-weight families (notation register §7aa: y_\lambda, w_\lambda and \tilde w_\lambda are distinct at q \neq 1). The body previously wrote it as w_\lambda(q), conflating it with the Ocneanu/Markov family; the title says \tilde w_\lambda, which is correct.
prop:confined-knot-binding:
Proposition Confined knot binding mechanism: character ratio decomposition per jet level. Let \beta \in H_3(R, q) be a confined nuclear braid built from crossing operators at generators \sigma_{i_k}. The Wedderburn-Artin decomposition separates each crossing's contribution into three channels:

  \hat{V}(c, d)
  = W_{\mathrm{sym}} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{sym}}(c, d)
  + W_{\mathrm{std}} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{std}}(c, d)
  + W_{\mathrm{alt}} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{alt}}(c, d).

The extremal contributions exactly cancel for symmetric crossings encoding the proton-neutron force. The binding volume transfers entirely to the standard representation:

  \hat{V}_{\mathrm{pn}}
  = W_{\mathrm{std}} \cdot \Bigl(z - \frac{h_{\mathrm{A}}}{2}\Bigr).

The 2-dimensional standard representation creates non-commuting cross-channel interactions between adjacent generators. This generates the Markov-weighted pair interaction term \delta_{\times}.

For an A-nucleon system constructed sequentially through quark, nucleon, and nuclear jet levels, the character ratio measures the volume departure from the free constituents. The total knot factor multiplies these strict, empirically-independent character ratios across all levels.
prf:confined-knot-binding:
Proof Proof of confined knot binding. The equality W_{\mathrm{sym}} = W_{\mathrm{alt}} follows from \dim_q(\lambda_{\mathrm{sym}}) = \dim_q(\lambda_{\mathrm{alt}}) = 1 for the one-dimensional representations of H_3(R, q). The Wedderburn weight is w_\lambda = d_q(\lambda)^2 / [n]_q!, and d_q((3)) = d_q((1,1,1)) = 1.

For the symmetric crossing (c, d) = (1, -h_{\mathrm{A}}/2):

  \chi_{\mathrm{sym}} + \chi_{\mathrm{alt}}
  = (q - h_{\mathrm{A}}/2) + (-q^{-1} - h_{\mathrm{A}}/2)
  = q - q^{-1} - h_{\mathrm{A}} = 0

since h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1}. Therefore the weighted sum vanishes: W_{\mathrm{sym}} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{sym}} + W_{\mathrm{alt}} \cdot \chi_{\mathrm{alt}} = W_{\mathrm{sym}}(\chi_{\mathrm{sym}} + \chi_{\mathrm{alt}}) = 0.

The standard-representation volume z - h_{\mathrm{A}}/2 follows from the transfer matrix with initial condition (a_0, b_0) = (0, 1): (a, b) = (1, -h_{\mathrm{A}}/2), giving \chi_{\mathrm{std}} = z \cdot 1 + (-h_{\mathrm{A}}/2) = z - h_{\mathrm{A}}/2.

For a general confined state at jet level \ell, the character ratio a_\ell compares the accumulated Wedderburn volume of the confined braid word against the tensor product of free constituent volumes. The product \prod_\ell a_\ell telescopes through the jet tower:

  \prod_\ell a_\ell
  = \frac{\hat{V}(\text{nucleus})}
         {\prod_{\text{nucleons}} \hat{V}(\text{nucleon})}
  \cdot
  \frac{\prod_{\text{nucleons}} \hat{V}(\text{nucleon})}
       {\prod_{\text{quarks}} \hat{V}(\text{quark})}
  \cdot \dotsb

Each factor is determined by the Hecke algebra multiplication rules applied to the crossing parameters at that level. \square
prop:molecular-bond-binding-from-trefoil:
Proposition Molecular bond binding energy from inverse-trefoil insertion. A covalent bond functions categorically as an inverse trefoil T^{-1} inserted between two atomic braids \mathcal{A} and \mathcal{B}. The molecular binding energy scales via the per-channel volume shifts:

  E_{\mathrm{bond}}
  = \bigl(
      W_{\mathrm{sym}} \cdot \Delta\Phi_{\mathrm{sym}}
    + W_{\mathrm{std}} \cdot \Delta\Phi_{\mathrm{std}}
    + W_{\mathrm{alt}} \cdot \Delta\Phi_{\mathrm{alt}}
    \bigr) \times E_{\mathrm{mol}},

where E_{\mathrm{mol}} = m_e \alpha^2 / 2 supplies the Hartree energy scale. Double and triple bonds insert multiple inverse trefoils, driving the 1 : 2 : 3 bond-energy scaling directly from the categorical multiplier.
prop:canonical-closure-torus-chain:
Proposition The canonical closure is a chain of (2,\mathrm{odd})-torus knots: bridge number 2A+1 and total curvature 2\pi(2A+1). Resolve each averaged letter of the canonical word of the atomic braid to a crossing sign (either branch) and freely reduce. The result is a chain form

  W_A \;=\; \prod_{k=0}^{A-1} \sigma_{3k}^{\,a_k}\,\sigma_{3k+1}^{\,b_k}\,\sigma_{3k+2}^{\,\varepsilon_k}
  \qquad(\text{no } \varepsilon \text{ on the last block}),

each generator appearing exactly once, in order, as a single power, with a_k odd, b_k even and non-zero, and \varepsilon_k = \pm 1. Consequently its closure is the linear connected sum of the torus links T(2, e_i) along shared strands: A knots T(2, a_k) and one unknot, consecutive components linked with \mathrm{lk} = b_k/2; the A-1 interface generators are connected-sum bands with the unknot and drop out, leaving the (2A+1)-strand chain W'_A = \prod_k \sigma_{2k}^{a_k}\sigma_{2k+1}^{b_k} with the same closure. Hence

  \mu = A+1,\qquad \#\{\text{knotted components}\} = A,\qquad b(L) = 2A+1,
  \qquad \inf_{\text{isotopy class}} \int \kappa\, ds \;=\; 2\pi\,(2A+1).
conj:jet-filtered-knot-factor:
Conjecture Jet-filtered knot factor: per-level character convergence and nuclear quotient braid. The Bethe-Weizsäcker knot factor a(Z, N) governing bulk binding evaluates directly from the jet-filtered character convergence of the nuclear quotient braid \bar\beta.

At higher jet levels, the per-level invariant converges strictly to a topology-independent q-dimension-weighted average. The intermediate nucleon-by-nucleon normal forms align with distinct knot patterns, mapping odd Z to trefoils and even Z to Hopf links. Double-magic nuclei converge strongly to the unknot.

The full bulk knot factor a(Z, N) equals the evaluated Jones polynomial of the nuclear quotient braid J_{\bar\beta}(q). The quotient tracks exclusively the A(A-1)/2 inter-nucleon crossings, suppressing internal nucleon structure.
conj:jet-convergence-classical-limit:
Conjecture Jet-filtered knot invariant converges to classical dimension-weighted average. At k = 3, the jet-filtered knot invariant evaluates exactly using the q-deformed Wedderburn weights W_\lambda = d_q(\lambda)^2 / [3]_q!. As the jet level k \to \infty, the invariant converges to the linear q-dimension scaling f_\mu^\infty = d_q(\mu)/\sum d_q(\nu).

The classical branching multiplicities remain q-independent, but the q-hook corrections do not factorize over the branching. The Kerov q-hook walk and the Féray-Méliot q-Plancherel Central Limit Theorem ensure O(1/\sqrt{k}) convergence. The q = 1 antecedent is Kerov's central limit theorem for Plancherel-random Young diagrams, in which the rescaled diagram fluctuates around the limit shape at order 1/\sqrt{n} [ivanov-olshanski2003, §7]. That order is the scale of the fluctuations, not a proved rate of convergence in distribution. For the normalised character ratio \tfrac{n-1}{\sqrt 2}\,\chi^{\lambda}(12)/\dim\lambda under Plancherel measure, the best proved Berry--Esseen bound is 40.1\,n^{-1/4}, with a bound of order n^{-1/2} conjectured [fulman2003, Thm. 1.2]. The O(1/\sqrt{k}) convergence stated above is therefore stronger than the proved q=1 distributional rate for this statistic, and is read here as a scale, not as a proved rate. The q-deformation critically enhances the standard channel at low k, explaining why the nuclear topology dominates binding exclusively at physical energy scales.
prop:wigner-np-pairing:
Proposition Wigner energy from T{=}0 np pairing: (2,2) partition at k{=}4. The self-conjugate (2,2) \vdash 4 partition at Hecke level k = 4 introduces the categorical Wigner energy from T=0 isoscalar np pairing. The energy scale equals exactly the (2,2) q-hook product:

  \mathbf{\Delta}_{(2,2)}
  = m_e \cdot [3]_q \cdot [2]_q^2
  \approx 6.29\;\mathrm{MeV}.

The scale matches the empirical Wigner value without fitting. The (2,2) channel and the bulk shell corrections derive from identical categorical dimensions. The unified iterative recursion subsumes this specific binding increment, accumulating the Wedderburn projection step-by-step from A=1.
prf:wigner-np-pairing:
Proof Proof of wigner np pairing. The partition (2,2) is self-conjugate (\lambda = \lambda'), with q-dimension d_q((2,2)) = [2]_q and Wedderburn weight w_{(2,2)} = [2]_q^2/[4]_q!.

By the branching rule H_4(R, q) \to H_3(R, q), the restriction of V_{(2,2)} contains only V_{(2,1)} (the standard representation) with multiplicity 1. Therefore the (2,2) contribution to binding is carried entirely by the standard channel, consistent with extremal cancellation for pn crossings (confined knot binding).

The scaling \min(Z, N)/A counts the maximum number of proton-neutron T{=}0 pairs per nucleon. Each pair contributes \hat{V}_{\mathrm{pn}} \cdot \alpha of binding through the standard channel.

The Kerov q-hook walk [kerov1996] provides the iterative construction: at each nucleon addition, the pn crossings project onto the (2,2) partition, accumulating the Wigner energy step by step from A = 1. The Féray–Méliot q-Plancherel CLT [feray-meliot2012] gives the asymptotic convergence rate O(1/\sqrt{k}) of the accumulator across Hecke levels. \square

prop:derived-mass-formula-light-isotopes:
Proposition Derived-only mass formula reproduces light atomic masses to sub-percent. The strict derived mass formula

\begin{aligned}
\mathfrak{m}(Z, N) &= Z \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} + N \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z m_e \\
                  &\quad + \alpha \bigl(\Phi_1 - 2[3]_q \Phi_2 + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3\bigr) \\
                  &\quad + \Delta_{W}(Z, N) + \Delta_{T=1}(Z, N)
\end{aligned}

with each term derived (no fitting):

  • \alpha = m_e \cdot 8G (Borromean prefactor; binding scale);
  • \Phi_1, \Phi_2, \Phi_3 extracted from per-generator transfer-matrix chains using only the inter-nucleon generators (positions 3k+2 for k = 0, \ldots, A{-}2);
  • \Delta_W = -m_e \cdot H_q((2,2)) \cdot \min(Z, N)/A (Wigner T=0 pn pairing, Wigner np pairing);
  • \Delta_{T=1} = -m_e \cdot H_q((2,2)) \cdot (n_{pp} + n_{nn})/A (natural T=1 isovector extension using the same self-conjugate partition (2,2) \vdash 4 and the same 1/A normalisation, with n_{pp} = Z(Z{-}1)/2 and n_{nn} = N(N{-}1)/2);

reproduces the atomic masses of all isotopes from \mathfrak{p} through ^7Li to sub-percent accuracy.

The categorical scorecard, the proton-neutron mass splitting, and the binding under-prediction pattern are collected in the derived-mass-formula scorecard.
